status: experimental interoperability architecture; no legal/treaty authority claim
purpose: Propagate bounded revocation, withdrawal, compromise, and recognition-narrowing signals across institutional trust domains while preserving historical reliance evidence and preventing remote notices from becoming local authority.
core_invariants: remote revocation or compromise evidence can invalidate future reliance but does not retroactively rewrite what was known at an earlier decision time
receipt of a remote notice does not itself authorize local punishment, remediation, or unrelated state changes
revocation scope must be exact: subject, claim class, key, verifier, recognition edge, policy, or institution
compromise of a root/trust anchor is a wider recovery class than compromise of one leaf/service key
withdrawal of recognition stops future reliance under that edge after the locally accepted effective time but preserves historical reliance receipts
stale or unverifiable revocation state is explicit and fails according to local consequence policy
offline nodes retain last-known status and reconcile later; they do not claim currentness they could not check
conflicting revocation/status assertions remain visible until local trust policy resolves them
cross-domain propagation is evidence distribution, not transitive authority

status_effects.use: may satisfy currentness checks if other policy conditions pass
deny or hold new reliance according to local policy
deny affected trust path and invoke appropriate recovery/revalidation
deny future reliance on the withdrawn recognition relationship
deny, hold, or downgrade to advisory according to local consequence policy

historical_rule: A reliance receipt records the exact evidence, recognition edge, policy, currentness state, and decision time. Later revocation annotates or supersedes future admissibility; it does not mutate the original receipt.
nonclaims: A remote revocation feed is not globally authoritative merely because it is signed.
Revocation does not automatically determine legal liability, fault, or remedy.
This profile does not define one global revocation network or consensus system.
A local institution may impose stricter currentness requirements.
